description:
Goal: make runtime module publication member-demanded instead of module-surface-demanded where the source model can support it. The fz-rh2.27 source/root ownership fix removed repeated prelude/user source publication, but the direct-lambda fz2 telemetry still shows that using `+` notes the whole Kernel source surface once: process intrinsics, arithmetic wrappers for unused operators, comparison/equality wrappers, `panic`, `dbg`, `assert`, `spawn`, `range`, and other unrelated functions/operators.

Grounding:
- Fresh fz2 telemetry after fz-rh2.27 shows the six prelude macro sources are now each noted once instead of four times, and the direct-lambda first drive dropped from 166 to 144 jobs.
- The remaining broad work is not a root-submission replay anymore; it is module-granularity runtime publication. `Kernel.+/2` and the add wrappers are reached, but the whole Kernel interface is noted when the Kernel module source is scoped.

Signal:
- A tiny program using only `+` should not emit `function.source.noted` for unrelated Kernel members such as `spawn`, `send`, `range`, `panic`, subtraction/multiplication/division/remainder wrappers, or comparison wrappers.
- Runtime module pull-through remains ordinary code and facts; no special runtime mode, no compatibility bridge.
- Tests assert presence and absence from telemetry: `Kernel.+/2` and required add extern wrappers are present; unrelated Kernel functions stay cold at source-publication, definition, lowering, activation, and transport/artifact tiers.

Strategy:
- First identify whether the right split is module-interface/member facts, exact import/require callable placeholders, or smaller runtime source contributions.
- Move the data-model boundary so a demanded runtime callable can publish the smallest needed surface without walking the whole runtime module.
- Update northstar-facing agent docs if the runtime module lifecycle gets a sharper member-publication tier.
title: Compiler2 runtime Kernel publication should be member-demanded
